questions.q: The chapter sizes a corpus of one million 2,000-token documents chunked at 512 tokens with 64-token overlap. Roughly how many chunks and how much raw vector data at 1536 dims does that produce?
options: About 20 million chunks and roughly 120 GB
About 500,000 chunks and roughly 3 GB
About 4.3 million chunks and roughly 25 GB of raw vector data
About 1 million chunks and roughly 6 GB
questions.explain: The chapter's sizing math: 512-token chunks with 64-token overlap over 1M x 2,000-token documents yields ~4.3M chunks, which at 1,536 dims is roughly 25 GB of raw vectors before indexing overhead.

questions.q: What overlap guidance does the chapter give, and why is 50% overlap a problem?
options: 10–15% overlap (50–64 tokens on a 512-token chunk) captures boundary context at modest cost; 50% overlap makes the index half-duplicate and lets near-duplicate vectors crowd out genuinely different content
50% overlap is the recommended default for all corpora
Overlap only matters for semantic splitting
Zero overlap is best; any overlap wastes storage
questions.explain: Overlap exists for boundary sentences: 10–15% captures boundary context cheaply, but 50% overlap means paying for an index that is half duplicate, with near-duplicates distorting the similarity ranking.

questions.q: How does parent-child retrieval combine small and large chunks?
options: Index large parent chunks (1,024+ tokens) for search, return small children (128–256 tokens) to the LLM
Index small child chunks (128–256 tokens) for precise similarity search, but return their larger parent chunks (1,024+ tokens) to the LLM for rich context
Store both and average their embeddings
It is just another name for fixed-size chunking
questions.explain: Parent-child retrieval indexes 128–256-token children for precision and returns the 1,024+-token parents for context — precise ranking plus rich context, with DISTINCT collapsing multiple child hits under one parent.

questions.q: Which chunking strategy does the chapter prescribe for code documents?
options: One chunk per row-group with headers repeated
Fixed 256-token chunks
One chunk per question-answer pair
Split on function/class boundaries, keep signatures with bodies, and never split mid-function
questions.explain: For code: split on function/class boundaries, keep signatures with bodies, store the file path and symbol name as metadata, and never split mid-function — the row-group rule is for tables, and Q&A pairing is for support articles.

questions.q: With a DiskANN index and highly selective metadata filters (eliminating more than ~90% of rows), what can outperform the ANN path?
options: Increasing TOP_N to 10,000
An exact VECTOR_DISTANCE scan with ORDER BY over the filtered subset
Removing the metadata filter entirely
Switching to binary quantization
questions.explain: The chapter states that for high-selectivity filters, an exact scan via VECTOR_DISTANCE + ORDER BY over the filtered subset often beats the filtered ANN path — measure both on your data (Chapter 20) rather than assuming the index always wins.
